cards.q: What types of Flexi Pension are there?
cards.a: Three: Retirement Phase, Transition to Retirement (TTR) and Beneficiary Income Stream (BIS). One PDS covers all three.

sources.quote: There's three types: Retirement Phase, Transition to Retirement (TTR) and Beneficiary Income Stream (BIS).

cards.q: Who can start a Retirement Phase Flexi Pension?
cards.a: Someone who has met a condition of release: 60+ and retired, left a job after 60, aged 65+ (even if working), or permanently incapacitated.

sources.quote: are aged 65 or over (even if you're still working), or

cards.q: Who can start a TTR Flexi Pension?
cards.a: Anyone who has reached preservation age and is still working. There's no minimum or maximum number of hours.

sources.quote: You can start a TTR Flexi Pension if you've reached your preservation age.* There's no minimum or maximum hours you need to work.

ato.quote: You reach your preservation age, continue working, and start a transition to retirement income stream.

cards.q: What's the minimum to start a Flexi Pension?

sources.quote: You need a minimum of $25,000 to start a Flexi Pension.

cards.q: Is there a maximum to start a Flexi Pension?
cards.a: Retirement Phase and BIS: limited by the member's personal transfer balance cap ($2.1 million for a first retirement income stream from 1 July 2026). TTR: no maximum.

sources.quote: Members starting their first retirement phase income stream with any super fund on or after 1 July 2026 will have a transfer balance cap of $2.1 million.

cards.q: How much has to stay in super when starting a pension from part of the balance?
cards.a: At least $6,000 must stay in the accumulation account (or DBD accumulation component). If the amount requested would leave less, we reduce the transfer.
cards.detail: Applies to a Retirement Phase pension from part of the balance and to every TTR pension.

sources.quote: If the amount you nominate to transfer would leave less than $6,000 in your account, we'll reduce the amount transferred to your Flexi Pension so that at least $6,000 remains in your account.

cards.q: Can money be added to a Flexi Pension after it starts?
cards.a: No. Once a pension starts nothing more can be added; it's a legal requirement. To add money, start a new pension account.
cards.detail: That's why members are encouraged to combine all their super before starting.

sources.quote: Once you start a Flexi Pension, you can't add further amounts to it. If you want to add money to an existing Flexi Pension account, you'll have to start a new account. This is a legal requirement.

cards.q: When does a Flexi Pension end?
aliases: how long will my pension last
cards.a: When the balance falls to $10,000, the rest is paid out: to the bank account (Retirement Phase, BIS) or to an accumulation account (TTR).

sources.quote: Your Flexi Pension will continue until the balance reduces to $10,000, after which the full balance will be paid to your nominated bank account (or an accumulation account for TTR Flexi Pension).

cards.q: What happens to insurance when the whole balance moves to a pension?
cards.a: Moving the entire accumulation account or component to a Retirement Phase pension ends any insurance cover.

sources.quote: If you transfer your entire accumulation account or component to a Retirement Phase Flexi Pension, any existing insurance cover you have will cease.

cards.q: Does a notice of intent need to be done before starting a pension?
cards.a: Yes. The notice must be lodged and acknowledged before the Retirement Phase or TTR pension is opened.

sources.quote: before opening your Retirement Phase or TTR Flexi Pension account.

cards.q: How does a member apply for a Flexi Pension?
cards.a: Online for existing Accumulation 1, Accumulation 2 and Personal Account members over 60 (Retirement Phase only). Everyone else uses the paper application from unisuper.com.au/pds.
cards.detail: TTR and BIS can't be applied for online.

sources.quote: Only available for UniSuper Accumulation 1, Accumulation 2 and Personal Account members over age 60.

cards.q: Does a member under 60 need a TFN declaration for a pension?
cards.a: Yes. An ATO Tax file number declaration for each Flexi Pension. From 60 a TFN isn't required.

sources.quote: If you're under age 60, you'll need to complete an ATO Tax file number declaration for each Flexi Pension you start.

cards.q: Is proof of identity needed to start a pension?
cards.a: Yes, before starting. It may also be asked for on lump sum withdrawals. It can be verified online with an Australian passport or driver licence.

sources.quote: you'll be required to provide proof of your identity before starting a Flexi Pension

cards.q: What is the temporary Accumulation 1 account?
cards.a: Opened to collect transfers when there's no active super account. No admin fees, invested in Cash, no insurance. Closes and the pension starts once all transfers are in, or 90 days after the first one, whichever is first.
cards.detail: Anything left after 90 days becomes a standard Accumulation 1 account with fees, or goes to the existing super account.

sources.quote: your account balance will be invested in the Cash investment option (and you won't be able to switch to another investment option)
or 90 days after we receive the first transfer or contribution, whichever happens first

cards.q: Can a member cancel a new pension?
cards.a: Within 14 days, in writing. Starts from the welcome letter or the fifth business day after opening, whichever is earlier. The balance is adjusted for market movements and payments made.
cards.detail: A TTR balance can't be paid to the member; it goes to super or another TTR provider. A BIS can't be paid to a super account.

sources.quote: To exercise your cooling-off right, you must advise us in writing within the cooling-off period.
If you opened a TTR Flexi Pension, we cannot pay your balance directly to you.

cards.q: What's the minimum pension payment percentage by age?
aliases: how much can a pensioner take out
how much do i have to take out
cards.a: Under 65: 4%. 65 to 74: 5%. 75 to 79: 6%. 80 to 84: 7%. 85 to 89: 9%. 90 to 94: 11%. 95+: 14%. Based on age at the start, then each 1 July.

sources.quote: Under 65 65 – 74 75 – 79 80 – 84 85 – 89 90 – 94 95 or older THE MINIMUM % OF YOUR BALANCE YOU MUST TAKE 4% 5% 6% 7% 9% 11% 14%
sources.label: Table: "Your age when you start your Flexi Pension and then every 1 July" against "The minimum % of your balance you must take"

ato.quote: This reduction has not been extended for the 2023–24 income year and onwards.

cards.q: How is the minimum payment worked out?
cards.a: Balance at the start of the financial year (or the opening balance) × the age percentage. It isn't recalculated if the member makes a withdrawal during the year.

sources.quote: The amount isn't recalculated if you make a withdrawal during the year.

ato.quote: Superannuation and annuity providers calculate the minimum annual payment required as at 1 July each year, based on the account balance of the member or annuitant.

cards.q: How is the first-year minimum pro-rated?
cards.a: Full-year minimum × days from the start date to 30 June ÷ days in the year, rounded to the nearest $10. Example: 67, $500,000, starts 1 Oct 2026: $25,000 × 273 ÷ 365 = $18,700.

sources.quote: Income payments in your first year are calculated in proportion to the number of days between your Flexi Pension account's opening date and the end of the financial year.
($18,698.63 rounded to the nearest $10)

ato.quote: the required minimum amount is calculated proportionately from the commencement day to the end of the financial year

cards.q: What if a pension starts in June?
cards.a: If it starts between 1 and 30 June, the member can choose not to receive a payment until the next financial year.

sources.quote: If you start your Flexi Pension between 1 June and 30 June, you can choose not to receive an income payment until the next financial year.

cards.q: Does a minimum still have to be paid if the pension closes mid-year?
cards.a: Yes, a minimum or pro-rata minimum may still need to be paid before a pension is commuted or closed during the year.

sources.quote: However, if you commute or close your Flexi Pension during the year, a minimum income payment (or a pro-rata minimum income payment) may still need to be paid.

cards.q: Do members get told their minimum each year?
cards.a: Yes. At the start of each financial year we tell the member the minimum; they then tell us how much they want, at least the minimum.

sources.quote: At the start of each financial year, we'll inform you of the minimum income amount you must draw from your Flexi Pension that year

cards.q: What payment frequencies are available?
cards.a: Fortnightly, monthly, quarterly (Mar, Jun, Sep, Dec), half-yearly (Jun, Dec) or annually (any month). Monthly if none is chosen.

sources.quote: quarterly (March, June, September and December)
If you don't nominate a frequency, you'll receive your payments monthly.

cards.q: When are pension payments paid?
cards.a: Fortnightly: by every second Friday. All other frequencies: by the 28th of the month. Some credit unions take longer to clear funds.

sources.quote: Payments are made into your nominated bank account(s) by every second Friday for fortnightly payments, or by the 28th of each month, for all other payment frequencies.

cards.q: How does a member change their payment amount, frequency or bank?
cards.a: Online: log in, Pension payments tab, Your payments. Or the Change of details or Change of bank account forms.

sources.quote: Log in to your account and select the `Your payments' option from the `pension payments' tab menu.

cards.q: What's the most a TTR pension can pay in a year?
cards.a: 10% of the balance at the start of the financial year, or of the opening balance in the first year. Recalculated each 1 July.

sources.quote: You can take up to a maximum of 10% of your account balance at the start of each financial year (or your initial account balance for the first year) as income payments.

cards.q: Is the TTR maximum pro-rated in the first year?
cards.a: No. The minimum is pro-rated but the 10% maximum isn't. Unless the member says otherwise, the year's income is spread over the months left (example: $40,000 from April = $13,330 a month).

sources.quote: The maximum amount for TTR Flexi Pension isn't subject to the pro-rata rules.
his annual income will be spread over the remaining three months

cards.q: Can a TTR member take a lump sum?
cards.a: Only in very limited cases: unrestricted non-preserved money, a family law split, or an ATO release authority.

sources.quote: accessing any unrestricted non-preserved benefits

cards.q: When does a TTR pension become Retirement Phase?
cards.a: Automatically at 65, or when the member tells us they've met a condition of release (such as retiring, or leaving a job after 60). Then full withdrawals are allowed and it counts towards the transfer balance cap.

sources.quote: Once you reach age 65 or let us know you've met a condition of release allowing unrestricted access to your super

cards.q: Which part of a TTR balance are payments drawn from first?
cards.a: Unrestricted non-preserved first, then restricted non-preserved, then preserved.

sources.quote: Your income payments and any lump sum withdrawals must be taken from your balance in the following order:

cards.q: Does a TTR pension affect insurance?
cards.a: Cover in the accumulation account continues as long as there's enough left to pay premiums and other conditions are met.

sources.quote: As long as you retain enough money in your accumulation account or component to pay for insurance premiums when due

cards.q: Are TTR earnings taxed?
cards.a: Yes, up to 15%, the same as super. Once it converts to Retirement Phase, earnings are tax-free.

sources.quote: Investment earnings on a TTR Flexi Pension can be subject to tax of up to 15%

cards.q: How does a member close a TTR pension?
cards.a: Transfer it back to a super account, or to another non-commutable income stream. Use the Transfer your Flexi Pension to a super account form, or call. A minimum or pro-rata minimum may need to be paid first.

sources.quote: To close your TTR Flexi Pension account, complete a Transfer your Flexi Pension to a super account application available on our website or by calling us.

cards.q: Can a pension member take a lump sum?
cards.a: Yes, at least $2,000 at any time if there's enough in the account. Usually paid within five business days.

sources.quote: You can make lump sum withdrawals of at least $2,000 from your Flexi Pension at any time if you have enough money in your account.

cards.q: What does commuting a pension mean?
cards.a: Converting all or part of it to a lump sum, to buy another account-based pension or move it to a super account. Advice is suggested.

sources.quote: You can also `commute' your Retirement Phase or TTR Flexi Pension (i.e. convert all or part of it to a lump sum)

cards.q: How does a member move a Retirement Phase pension back to super?
cards.a: Transfer your Flexi Pension to a super account form, or call. It's invested in the rollover strategy, or Balanced if none. With no active super account, a new Accumulation 1 account is opened.

sources.quote: If you don't have a rollover strategy, it will be invested in our default Balanced (MySuper) investment option.

cards.q: Who can start a BIS Flexi Pension?
cards.a: Only the spouse of a deceased member who is entitled to a super death benefit, from UniSuper or another fund.

sources.quote: You can only start a BIS Flexi Pension if you're entitled to receive a super death benefit and you're the spouse of the deceased.

cards.q: How is a BIS Flexi Pension set up?
cards.a: Lodge the death benefit claim (with UniSuper or the other fund) and say you want a BIS. Then complete the BIS Flexi Pension application.

sources.quote: When lodging the death benefit claim, tell us that you'd like to start a BIS Flexi Pension by rolling all or part of the death benefit into it.

cards.q: What are the BIS restrictions?
cards.a: Can't be combined with other super, can't have a reversionary beneficiary, and is paid only as income or a cash lump sum. It counts towards the transfer balance cap.

sources.quote: A BIS Flexi Pension, started with a super death benefit, can't be combined with other money you have in super.
If you're applying for a BIS Flexi Pension, then you can't make a reversionary beneficiary nomination.

cards.q: What return applies before a BIS starts?
cards.a: From a UniSuper accumulation or pension member: the Cash option return from when we're notified of the death. From a DBD member: generally the Cash return from when they ceased service.

sources.quote: we'll apply the rate of return of our Cash investment option from the date we're notified of the death until the account is closed to establish your pension

cards.q: How is a BIS pension closed?
cards.a: Log in or call. The balance is paid as cash to the nominated bank account, unless used for another BIS or rolled to another fund's death benefit income stream.

sources.quote: To close your BIS Flexi Pension, log in to your online account or call us.

cards.q: What is the transfer balance cap?
cards.a: A lifetime limit on how much can be moved into retirement-phase pensions across all funds. Personal caps are between $1.6 million and $2.1 million; $2.1 million for a first pension from 1 July 2026.
cards.detail: The ATO tracks it. The member checks their cap with the ATO or ato.gov.au online services.

sources.quote: Each member will have their own personal transfer balance cap between $1.6 million and $2.1 million, depending on their circumstances.
To view your transfer balance cap and your transfer balance account, please contact the ATO

ato.quote: It is a limit on the total amount of superannuation that can be transferred into the retirement phase.

cards.q: What happens if a member goes over the transfer balance cap?
cards.a: The excess and notional earnings must be removed; the ATO says how much. Tax on notional earnings is 15% for a first breach, 30% after. If the member does nothing, the fund must reduce the balance within 60 days of the ATO's notice.

sources.quote: The tax rate is 15% for the first breach and increases to 30% for any further breaches.
require that reduction be made within 60 days

cards.q: Does a TTR pension count towards the transfer balance cap?
cards.a: Not until it's in retirement phase: at 65 or once a condition of release is reported.

sources.quote: does not apply to TTR income streams (until you reach age 65 or you inform us that you've met a specified condition of release).

cards.q: Does the transfer balance cap go up?
cards.a: The general cap is indexed to CPI in $100,000 steps. Investment returns don't count as credits towards the transfer balance account.

sources.quote: over time in line with the Consumer Price Index (CPI) in $100,000 increments

cards.q: What is the Retirement Bonus?
cards.a: Tax savings that may be passed on when money moves into a Retirement Phase pension (capital gains tax set aside is no longer needed). It's added automatically; no application.
cards.detail: Rate, maximum and eligible options: unisuper.com.au/retirement-bonus.

sources.quote: You don't need to apply. The Retirement Bonus will be added automatically to your Retirement Phase Flexi Pension when it starts.

cards.q: Who gets the Retirement Bonus?
cards.a: Members transferring super or TTR to a Retirement Phase pension from 1 October 2026, with money in eligible options, who've held a UniSuper super or TTR account for 12 continuous months before the transfer.

sources.quote: have held a UniSuper super and/or TTR Flexi Pension account for a continuous 12-month period immediately before the transfer

cards.q: Can the Retirement Bonus be taken back?
cards.a: Yes. Withdrawing 50% or more of the opening balance within 12 months of starting may mean the bonus is clawed back.

sources.quote: If you withdraw 50% or more of your opening balance within 12 months of starting your Retirement Phase Flexi Pension, the Trustee may claw back the Retirement Bonus.

cards.q: Does the Retirement Bonus count towards caps?
cards.a: Not towards contribution caps (it isn't a contribution), but yes towards the transfer balance cap. Payment is at the Trustee's discretion and can change or stop.

sources.quote: Yes, the Retirement Bonus counts towards your transfer balance cap
Payment of the Retirement Bonus is at the Trustee's discretion

cards.q: Which investment options are pension payments taken from?
cards.a: Three choices: Default order (Cash first, then Australian Bond, Conservative and so on), Your choice (member sets the order), or Pro-rata (in proportion to each option). Changeable online any time.

sources.quote: then you can choose where your income payments (and lump sum withdrawals) come from

cards.q: Where is a pension invested if no choice is made?
cards.a: The default Balanced option. There are 16 options to choose from.

sources.quote: Your Flexi Pension account will automatically be invested in our default Balanced investment option.

cards.q: Are pension payments taxed?
cards.a: From 60, payments and lump sums are tax-free. Under 60, the taxable component is taxed at marginal rates; a 15% offset may apply for a disability super benefit.

sources.quote: All retirement income payments and lump sum withdrawals are paid tax-free.
If you're under age 60 you may be eligible for a 15% tax offset if you're receiving a disability super benefit.

cards.q: How is a pension lump sum taxed under 60?
cards.a: It's drawn proportionally from taxable and tax-free components. The taxable component is taxed at up to 22% (including Medicare) with a TFN.

sources.quote: Any lump sum withdrawal you make must include taxable and tax-free components in the same proportions as your entire benefit.

cards.q: How does Centrelink treat a Flexi Pension?
cards.a: The whole balance counts for the assets test, and deeming generally applies for the income test. UniSuper sends Centrelink schedules directly.
cards.detail: For changes to the tests, refer to UniSuper Advice (1800 823 842) or servicesaustralia.gov.au.

sources.quote: Your entire Flexi Pension account balance will count towards the assets test and Centrelink deeming rates will generally be applied
We regularly produce Centrelink schedules and provide these directly to Centrelink as a service to our members.

cards.q: What are the Flexi Pension fees?
cards.a: Retirement Phase and BIS: $96 a year ($8 a month) plus 0.08% a year, capped at $1,250. TTR: no admin fee while under TTR rules. Balanced investment fee 0.32% (TTR 0.39%), transaction costs 0.06%.
cards.detail: On $50,000 in Balanced: $326 a year (Retirement Phase), $225 (TTR).

sources.quote: 0.08% of your account balance per year, capped at $1,250 per account per financial year.
that year you will be charged fees and costs of $326 for the superannuation product.

cards.q: What happens to DBD membership when the DB component is used for a pension?
cards.a: The DBD account closes and can't be rejoined. Inbuilt benefits stop. Using only the accumulation component keeps DBD membership.

sources.quote: If you use all or part of your DB component to start a Flexi Pension, then your DBD account will be closed. You won't be eligible to rejoin the DBD.
If you're a DBD member and only use your accumulation component to start a Flexi Pension, then you'll remain a DBD member

cards.q: What if a DBD member is 65+ when starting a Retirement Phase pension?
cards.a: They're treated as having deferred the DB component. Anything not used for the pension goes to an Accumulation 1 account.

sources.quote: we'll regard you as having elected to defer your DB component

cards.q: Can a temporary resident start a Flexi Pension?
cards.a: Generally only for a terminal medical condition, permanent incapacity, or a condition of release met before 1 April 2009.

sources.quote: you can generally only start a Flexi Pension under the following limited circumstances

cards.q: Are pension payments guaranteed?
cards.a: No. Payments stop when there isn't enough for the next one, and the rest is paid out. Withdrawals and returns affect how long it lasts.

sources.quote: Income payments will stop when you no longer have enough money in your pension account to meet the next payment.
